$comment: Nissan SR20DET, the S-chassis launch swap. Researched 2026-09-26. Top-level hardware is shared by the S13/S14/S15 longitudinal SR20DET; per-market and per-gearbox ratings are variants. The S15 automatic (225 PS) and the Australian 200SX (147 kW) are real, separately rated variants. Primary engine data comes from the Japanese catalogue databases, Nissan's 1999 launch release, the English S14 service manual and Nissan's parts catalogue (EPC, read at megazip.net, Japan-market builds only). No S15 service manual could be opened (the English S15 workshop manual on silviaoc.com needs a login, and no Japanese 整備要領書 or 新型車解説書 was found online), so S14 FSM values are labelled as such; where the EPC shows the S15 uses the same Nissan part as the S14 (camshafts, automatic injectors), the note says so.

dryWeight.note: Weak source: an enthusiast blog quoting a table of unknown origin (the same table is re-posted on ameblo.jp/blogorido, which says it probably includes ancillaries such as the turbo). It is not stated whether this is dry or with fluids. The English S14 service manual gives no engine weight (searched in full), and the S15 manual could not be opened. enginetechspecs.com prints 140 kg but that page contains clear errors (e.g. six main bearings; the FSM says five), and low-offset.com says only 'the SR20 is 400 lbs' with no source or condition, so neither was used. No Nissan figure was found; treat this as the best available, not as fact.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Nissan SR engine
sources.note: SR20DE specification table (headed 'SAE, 1991'): 'Dimensions: 685 mm x 610 mm x 615 mm'.

length.method: No SR20DET outline dimensions were found in any Nissan source that could be opened: the English S14 service manual (GI, MA, EM, LC and EC sections searched) gives none, the S15 manual could not be opened, and no Nissan Technical Review or SAE paper text was reachable. Used the SR20DE base-engine envelope from Wikipedia's SR20DE table (credited to SAE, 1991), taking the three figures in the order printed as length x width x height. The order is not labelled in the source, the SR20DE is an early transverse NA engine, and the RWD SR20DET adds a turbo and exhaust manifold on one side, so width in particular is likely larger. enginetechspecs.com prints 610 x 640 x 680 mm for the SR20DET with no source (and errors elsewhere on the page), so it was not used.

width.method: Second figure of the SR20DE 'Dimensions' entry (Wikipedia, credited to SAE 1991), assumed to be width. No Nissan SR20DET figure was found (S14 FSM searched; S15 manual not openable). The SR20DET's turbo, exhaust manifold and intake plenum are not included, so the real SR20DET width is probably larger. enginetechspecs.com (unsourced, unreliable) prints 640 mm.

bellhousing.note: The RWD SR20 bell pattern is shared by the SR20DE and SR20DET (Thrash Garage). sources.title: Nissan Service Manual, Model S14 Series (English, (c)1994 Nissan), SR20DET, section EM (Oil pan; Cylinder block), hosted by sr20tuning.net
sources.note: EM-14, figure SEM976E (underside view, 'Engine front' arrow pointing left): the steel oil pan opening, with the baffle plate and the oil strainer, sits directly behind the crankshaft pulley. EM-57, figure SEM036F: the oil strainer (5) bolts up beside the front cover with oil pump (4). EM-13, figure SEM974E: the deep section of the aluminium upper pan is drawn at the alternator-bracket (front) end, with the transmission-mounting flange at the other end. EM-14 text: removing the aluminium pan needs the front suspension member lowered 'by around 60 mm'; the steel pan comes off without that.

sources.title: Eat sleep BOOST: SR20DET tech info
sources.note: 'S14/S15 updated oil pickup – 15050-65F01': the S14 and S15 SR20DET share the oil pickup, so the S14 pan layout applies to the S15. (This page does not state the sump position.)

sump.note: Read from labelled FSM drawings; the manual never says 'front sump' in words, and the S15 manual could not be opened. This corrects an earlier reading of the same manual as a rear sump: in the EM-13 exploded view the steel pan and baffle plate are drawn off to one side, but the EM-14 underside view shows them fitted right behind the crank pulley. A front sump also fits the aftermarket selling 'rear sump' SR20DET pans for 240Z/510 swaps (seen in search results only; those pages returned 403 and are not cited).

sources.title: NSB Concept: Forged connecting rods Nissan 2.0L 16V Turbo SR20DET
sources.note: 'as soon as boost pressure and engine speed rise, the factory sintered-steel rods become the first weak link to address.'

rods.note: UNRESOLVED. What each source says: NSB Concept (French parts retailer, the only opened page that names a material) says 'factory sintered-steel rods'. The S14 service manual gives rod dimensions and bearing clearances but no material. The RODEX engine-builder blog (rodex.blog.fc2.com, entry 229, the source Japanese Wikipedia cites) says S15 engines built in 2002 switched to the X-Trail SR20VET rod (different small end) and that the X-Trail rod is machined rather than left as-cast, but does not say forged or sintered. Forum snippets claiming forged rods (nicoclub.com, sr20forum.com) could not be opened. No Nissan document was found. Check before the sim uses rod material for strength.

sources.title: High Performance Academy: Everything You Need to Know About the SR20DET
sources.note: 'Factory SR20DET pistons are only good for around 400hp at the wheels'; 'the stock pistons are fairly weak'.

pistons.method: No opened source states the stock SR20DET piston material outright; the S14 service manual gives piston dimensions only. Tomei's SR20DET piston page contrasts its forged pistons with productivity-first cast production pistons, and HPA calls the stock pistons weak. RODEX says the piston design changed along with the 2002 rod change. Search snippets (not openable) describe them as cast hypereutectic. 'cast' is inferred from these, not read from a Nissan document.

sources.note: Page 2: 'Koji tuned the S15 at stock boost levels 9psi (0.65bar) first.' Page 3: 'closer examination of the baseline boost curve showed boost-creep that actually took the stock boost levels from 9psi up to 12psi.' Page 1 describes the engine as the one 'Nissan rated … to produce 250PS' (the 6MT rating).

boost.note: One magazine test of one JDM 2001 S15 (gearbox not stated), not a Nissan figure; Nissan releases give no boost and the S15 manual could not be opened. English Wikipedia's table says '7psi stock' without a citation; Australian Car.Reviews gives 0.73 bar (10.6 psi) peak for the Australian 200SX (see s15-audm). The ECU sets boost through a duty-controlled wastegate solenoid with maps chosen by fuel octane and gear (S14 FSM EC-30, same system), so the figure varies with conditions.
